evidence_items.value: Population-based case-control analysis using rare variant burden testing in three biobanks (All of Us, UK Biobank, Mass General Brigham Biobank) with 748,879 individuals, testing gene-level associations with HCM defined by ICD-10 code I42.2.

source.text_snippet: We utilized a publicly available, online browser-based, phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) database which tested the association of rare coding variants with multiple phenotypes in 748,879 individuals across these three large biobanks (All of Us, UK biobank, Mass General Brigham biobank), 155,236 of which are of non-European ancestry [ 16 ]. This dataset was limited to gene-level analysis and does not provide data on specific variants. The analysis was specified to rare variants (minor allele frequency <0.001) and the one ICD-10 phenocode available for HCM (“I42.2—Other hypertrophic cardiomyopathy”) in this PheWAS database.

raw_source.text_snippet: We utilized a publicly available, online browser-based, phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) database which tested the association of rare coding variants with multiple phenotypes in 748,879 individuals across these three large biobanks (All of Us, UK biobank, Mass General Brigham biobank), 155,236 of which are of non-European ancestry [ 16 ]. This dataset was limited to gene-level analysis and does not provide data on specific variants. The analysis was specified to rare variants (minor allele frequency <0.001) and the one ICD-10 phenocode available for HCM (“I42.2—Other hypertrophic cardiomyopathy”) in this PheWAS database.

evidence_items.notes: The study design is a population-based genetic association study using rare variant burden testing at the gene level. This is relevant for assessing gene-disease association for MT-TI and HCM, though MT-TI is in the moderate group and was not specifically highlighted in the results.
inference_basis: General population-based genetic association study design.

evidence_items.value: Rare variant burden testing using six masks (LOF, missense with various thresholds) and Cauchy combination of p-values; Bonferroni correction for 38 genes (threshold p<0.00132).

source.text_snippet: A two-sided p value < 0.05 was considered nominally significant. We specifically used the cauchy p value provided by the PheWAS, which integrates the p values from all six rare burden testing masks into one. However, we also applied a Bonferroni correction to account for multiple-gene testing for 38 genes, whereby the adjusted p value threshold ( p adj ) was <0.00132 (0.05/38 genes).

raw_source.text_snippet: A two-sided p value < 0.05 was considered nominally significant. We specifically used the cauchy p value provided by the PheWAS, which integrates the p values from all six rare burden testing masks into one. However, we also applied a Bonferroni correction to account for multiple-gene testing for 38 genes, whereby the adjusted p value threshold ( p adj ) was <0.00132 (0.05/38 genes).

evidence_items.notes: The statistical method is described for the overall study. It is not specific to MT-TI but applies to all genes tested.
